            <summary>
            A delegating chat client that invokes functions defined on <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.ChatOptions"/>.
            Include this in a chat pipeline to resolve function calls automatically.
            </summary>
            <remarks>
            <para>
            When this client receives a <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.FunctionCallContent"/> in a chat response from its inner
            <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.IChatClient"/>, it responds by invoking the corresponding <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.AIFunction"/> defined
            in <see cref="P:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.ChatOptions.Tools"/> (or in <see cref="P:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.FunctionInvokingChatClient.AdditionalTools"/>), producing a <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.FunctionResultContent"/>
            that it sends back to the inner client. This loop is repeated until there are no more function calls to make, or until
            another stop condition is met, such as hitting <see cref="P:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.FunctionInvokingChatClient.MaximumIterationsPerRequest"/>.
            </para>
            <para>
            If a requested function is an <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.AIFunctionDeclaration"/> but not an <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.AIFunction"/>, the
            <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.FunctionInvokingChatClient"/> will not attempt to invoke it, and instead allow that <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.FunctionCallContent"/>
            to pass back out to the caller. It is then that caller's responsibility to create the appropriate <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.FunctionResultContent"/>
            for that call and send it back as part of a subsequent request.
            </para>
            <para>
            Further, if a requested function is an <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.ApprovalRequiredAIFunction"/>, the <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.FunctionInvokingChatClient"/> will not
            attempt to invoke it directly. Instead, it will replace that <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.FunctionCallContent"/> with a <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.ToolApprovalRequestContent"/>
            that wraps the <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.FunctionCallContent"/> and indicates that the function requires approval before it can be invoked. The caller is then
            responsible for responding to that approval request by sending a corresponding <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.ToolApprovalResponseContent"/> in a subsequent
            request. The <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.FunctionInvokingChatClient"/> will then process that approval response and invoke the function as appropriate.
            </para>
            <para>
            Due to the nature of interactions with an underlying <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.IChatClient"/>, if any <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.FunctionCallContent"/> is received
            for a function that requires approval, all received <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.FunctionCallContent"/> in that same response will also require approval,
            even if they were not <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.ApprovalRequiredAIFunction"/> instances. If this is a concern, consider requesting that multiple tool call
            requests not be made in a single response, by setting <see cref="P:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.ChatOptions.AllowMultipleToolCalls"/> to <see langword="false"/>.
            </para>
            <para>
            A <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.FunctionInvokingChatClient"/> instance is thread-safe for concurrent use so long as the
            <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.AIFunction"/> instances employed as part of the supplied <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.ChatOptions"/> are also safe.
            The <see cref="P:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.FunctionInvokingChatClient.AllowConcurrentInvocation"/> property can be used to control whether multiple function invocation
            requests as part of the same request are invocable concurrently, but even with that set to <see langword="false"/>
            (the default), multiple concurrent requests to this same instance and using the same tools could result in those
            tools being used concurrently (one per request). For example, a function that accesses the HttpContext of a specific
            ASP.NET web request should only be used as part of a single <see cref="T:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.ChatOptions"/> at a time, and only with
            <see cref="P:Microsoft.Extensions.AI.FunctionInvokingChatClient.AllowConcurrentInvocation"/> set to <see langword="false"/>, in case the inner client decided to issue multiple
            invocation requests to that same function.
            </para>
            </remarks>
        </member>

## Complete API Summary: .NET 10 AI Agent & Tool Calling

I've analyzed all four NuGet packages. Here's a comprehensive guide for building AI agents with tool calling in .NET 10:

---

## **1. CORE ABSTRACTIONS** (`Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Abstractions`)

### **IChatClient Interface** - Core chat interaction
- **Primary Methods:**
  - `GetResponseAsync(IEnumerable<ChatMessage>, ChatOptions, CancellationToken)` - Non-streaming chat
  - `GetStreamingResponseAsync(IEnumerable<ChatMessage>, ChatOptions, CancellationToken)` - Streaming chat
  - `GetService(Type, object)` - Access underlying services

### **ChatMessage** - Individual message in conversation
- Constructors:
  - `ChatMessage()` - defaults to User role
  - `ChatMessage(ChatRole role, string content)` - simple text
  - `ChatMessage(ChatRole role, IList<AIContent> contents)` - rich content
- Properties: `Role`, `AuthorName`, `CreatedAt`, `Content`, `RawRepresentation`

### **ChatRole** - Message sender type
- Static properties: `System`, `Assistant`, `User`, `Tool`

### **ChatOptions** - Configuration for chat requests
- **Core Properties:**
  - `ModelId` - Model identifier
  - `Temperature` - Randomness (0-1, lower = deterministic)
  - `TopP` - Nucleus sampling (0-1)
  - `TopK` - Top-k tokens to consider
  - `MaxOutputTokens` - Max response length
  - `StopSequences` - When to stop generation
- **Tool/Function Calling:**
  - `Tools` - `IList<AITool>` - Tools available to the model
  - `AllowMultipleToolCalls` - Allow multiple functions per response
- **Advanced:**
  - `Instructions` - Per-request system instructions
  - `ConversationId` - Link to existing conversation
  - `AllowBackgroundResponses` - For long-running ops
  - `RawRepresentationFactory` - Custom underlying options

### **ChatResponse** - Response from chat client
- Properties:
  - `Messages` - `IList<ChatMessage>` response messages
  - `Text` - Concatenated text of all messages
  - `ResponseId` - Response identifier
  - `ConversationId` - Conversation state identifier
  - `FinishReason` - Why response ended (Stop, Length, ToolCalls, etc.)

---

## **2. FUNCTION CALLING & TOOLS** (`Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Abstractions`)

### **AITool** - Base tool representation
- Properties: `Name`, `Description`, `AdditionalProperties`
- Method: `GetService<T>(object serviceKey)` - Access underlying tool

### **AIFunctionDeclaration** - Describes a function the model can call
- Properties:
  - `JsonSchema` - JSON Schema describing function and inputs
  - `ReturnJsonSchema` - JSON Schema for return value

### **AIFunction : AIFunctionDeclaration** - Invocable function
- Properties:
  - `UnderlyingMethod` - `MethodInfo` for .NET methods
  - `JsonSerializerOptions` - For parameter marshaling
- Methods:
  - `InvokeAsync(AIFunctionArguments, CancellationToken)` - Execute function
  - `InvokeCoreAsync(...)` - Core implementation
  - `AsDeclarationOnly()` - Get declaration-only version

### **AIFunctionFactory** - Create functions from delegates/methods
- **Key Methods:**
  - `Create(Delegate, AIFunctionFactoryOptions)` - From delegate
  - `Create(Delegate, string name, string description, JsonSerializerOptions)` - With custom metadata
  - `Create(MethodInfo, object target, AIFunctionFactoryOptions)` - From MethodInfo
- **Special Handling:**
  - `CancellationToken` parameters auto-bound (not in schema)
  - `IServiceProvider` parameters sourced from `AIFunctionArguments.Services`

### **AIFunctionArguments** - Function call parameters
- Dictionary of name/value pairs for function arguments
- Property: `Services` - `IServiceProvider` for dependency injection

### **FunctionCallContent** - Model requests function execution
- Constructor: `FunctionCallContent(string callId, string name, IDictionary<string, object> arguments)`
- Properties: `Name`, `Arguments`, `CallId`, `Exception`

### **FunctionResultContent** - Return value from function execution
- Constructor: `FunctionResultContent(string callId, object result)`
- Properties: `Result`, `Exception`, `CallId`

---

## **3. FUNCTION INVOKING CLIENT** (`Microsoft.Extensions.AI`)

### **FunctionInvokingChatClient** - Automatic tool call handling
- **Purpose:** Intercepts `FunctionCallContent`, invokes tools, returns results
- **Constructor:** `FunctionInvokingChatClient(IChatClient innerClient, ILoggerFactory loggerFactory, IServiceProvider functionInvocationServices)`
- **Key Properties:**
  - `MaximumIterationsPerRequest` - Max tool call rounds (default: 40)
  - `MaximumConsecutiveErrorsPerRequest` - Error tolerance (default: 3)
  - `AllowConcurrentInvocation` - Concurrent function execution
  - `IncludeDetailedErrors` - Detailed error messages in history
  - `CurrentContext` - `FunctionInvocationContext` for current call
- **Loop Behavior:** Automatically cycles request → tool call → result → request until no more calls or limit reached

### **FunctionInvocationContext** - Context during execution
- Tracks current function invocation state

---

## **4. CHAT CLIENT BUILDER PATTERN** (`Microsoft.Extensions.AI`)

### **ChatClientBuilder** - Pipeline construction
- **Constructors:**
  - `ChatClientBuilder(IChatClient innerClient)` - Start with client
  - `ChatClientBuilder(Func<IServiceProvider, IChatClient>)` - Start with factory
- **Methods:**
  - `Build(IServiceProvider)` - Create final pipeline client
  - `Use(Func<IChatClient, IChatClient>)` - Add middleware
  - `Use(Func<IChatClient, IServiceProvider, IChatClient>)` - Middleware with DI
  - `Use(Func<...ChatMessage/ChatOptions...>)` - Custom delegate pipeline

**Common Middleware Available:**
- `FunctionInvokingChatClientBuilderExtensions.UseFunctionInvoking()` - Add function calling
- `LoggingChatClientBuilderExtensions.UseLogging()` - Add logging
- `CachingChatClient` - Response caching
- `ReducingChatClient` - Message history reduction
- `ConfigureOptionsChatClient` - Custom option configuration

---

## **5. OPENAI INTEGRATION** (`Microsoft.Extensions.AI.OpenAI`)

### **Creating OpenAI Chat Clients**
```csharp
// From OpenAI.Chat.ChatClient
IChatClient client = openAiChatClient.AsIChatClient();

// From OpenAI.Responses.ResponsesClient
IChatClient client = responsesClient.AsIChatClient();

// From OpenAI.Assistants.AssistantClient
IChatClient client = assistantClient.AsIChatClient(assistantId, threadId);
IChatClient client = assistantClient.AsIChatClient(assistant, threadId);
```

### **OpenAI Client Adapters:**
- **OpenAIChatClient** - Maps `IChatClient` → OpenAI Chat API
- **OpenAIResponsesChatClient** - Maps `IChatClient` → OpenAI Responses API
- **OpenAIAssistantsChatClient** - Maps `IChatClient` → OpenAI Assistants API

### **Extension Methods:**
- `AsOpenAIChatTool(AIFunctionDeclaration)` - Convert function to OpenAI tool
- `AsOpenAIChatMessages(IEnumerable<ChatMessage>, ChatOptions)` - Convert messages
- `AsOpenAIChatCompletion(ChatResponse)` - Convert response

---

## **6. AGENT FRAMEWORK** (`Microsoft.Agents.AI`)

### **ChatClientAgent** - High-level agent orchestration
- **Constructor:**
  ```csharp
  ChatClientAgent(
      IChatClient chatClient,
      string instructions,           // System instructions
      string name,                   // Agent name
      string description,            // Agent description
      IList<AITool> tools,          // Available tools
      ILoggerFactory loggerFactory,  // Logging
      IServiceProvider services      // DI services
  )
  ```

- **Run Methods:**
  - `RunAsync(string message, AgentSession, ChatClientAgentRunOptions, CancellationToken)` - Single message
  - `RunAsync(ChatMessage message, ...)` - Chat message
  - `RunAsync(IEnumerable<ChatMessage> messages, ...)` - Multiple messages
  - `RunAsync(AgentSession, ChatClientAgentRunOptions, CancellationToken)` - No message
  - `RunStreamingAsync(...)` - Streaming variant

- **Returns:** `AgentResponse` with messages and metadata

### **ChatClientAgentRunOptions** - Agent execution config
- **Constructor:** `ChatClientAgentRunOptions(ChatOptions chatOptions)`
- **Properties:**
  - `ChatOptions` - `ChatOptions` to merge with agent defaults
  - `ChatClientFactory` - Custom client factory for this run

### **ChatClientAgentSession** - Conversation state
- Maintains message history across runs
- Used for stateful agent conversations

### **AIAgentBuilder** - Agent pipeline construction
- Similar to `ChatClientBuilder` but for agents
- Methods: `Build()`, `Use(Func<AIAgent, AIAgent>)`, etc.

---

## **7. KEY PATTERNS FOR BUILDING AN AGENT**

### **Pattern 1: Direct Chat Client with Function Calling**
```
Create OpenAI ChatClient
  ↓
Convert to IChatClient via .AsIChatClient()
  ↓
Create AIFunctions from methods via AIFunctionFactory
  ↓
Wrap with FunctionInvokingChatClient (automatic loop)
  ↓
Create ChatOptions with .Tools = [AIFunctions]
  ↓
Call GetResponseAsync() - automatic tool invocation loop
```

### **Pattern 2: High-Level Agent**
```
Create ChatClientAgent with:
  - IChatClient (OpenAI or other)
  - Instructions (system prompt)
  - Tools (AIFunctions)
  ↓
Create ChatClientAgentSession for state
  ↓
Call RunAsync(message, session, options)
  - Agent handles tool calls internally
  - Session tracks history
  - Returns AgentResponse
```

### **Pattern 3: Pipelined Clients**
```
ChatClientBuilder(openAiClient.AsIChatClient())
  .UseFunctionInvoking(loggerFactory, services)  // Add tool calling
  .UseLogging(loggerFactory)                      // Add logging
  .UseConfigureOptions(...)                       // Custom config
  .Build(services)
```

---

## **8. TOOL MODES** (`Microsoft.Extensions.AI`)

**ChatToolMode Options:**
- `AutoChatToolMode` - Automatic function calling (most common)
- `RequiredChatToolMode` - Model must use a tool
- `NoneChatToolMode` - No tool use allowed

---

## **9. MESSAGE CONTENT TYPES**

Beyond text, ChatMessage supports:
- `TextContent` - Plain text
- `FunctionCallContent` - Model requests function execution
- `FunctionResultContent` - Function execution result
- `ImageContent` - Images
- `CodeInterpreterToolCallContent` / `CodeInterpreterToolResultContent`
- `WebSearchToolCallContent` / `WebSearchToolResultContent`
- Custom `AIContent` subclasses

---

## **10. CRITICAL SECURITY NOTES** (from docs)
- LLM output is **untrusted** - validate before using
- Tool arguments are **untrusted input** - sanitize appropriately
- Enable **tool approval** for sensitive operations
- Default = all tools invoked without approval
- Use `ApprovalRequiredAIFunction` for sensitive tools

---

This gives you everything needed to build AI agents with function calling in .NET 10! The key is: `ChatClientBuilder` + `FunctionInvokingChatClient` + `AIFunctionFactory` creates a complete agent loop, or use `ChatClientAgent` for higher-level orchestration.
